title: Caesar Cipher
story: Julius Caesar sent secret military messages by shifting each letter three positions: A→D, B→E, C→F. Two thousand years later, it's still the most famous cipher in history. Build an encoder AND decoder — learn how cryptography begins.
why: The Caesar cipher teaches character manipulation, modulo arithmetic for wrapping, and the fundamental concept of reversible transformations.
analogy: A decoder ring from a cereal box: you rotate the outer ring (shift) and suddenly A maps to G, B to H. Your Caesar cipher function IS the decoder ring — set the shift, and the entire alphabet rotates. Crack one letter and you crack them all.
try_it: Encrypt a full sentence with punctuation and spaces. Try all 25 possible shifts and print each — you've built a brute-force cracker. What shift decodes 'Khoor Zruog'? Implement `crack_caesar` that tries all shifts and returns the most likely English-looking result.
tips: Decryption is just encryption with the negative shift
Handle both uppercase and lowercase separately — they wrap independently
common_mistakes: Not handling negative shifts properly — add 26 before modulo to fix: (pos + shift + 26) % 26
Forgetting that Char arithmetic produces Int — must cast back with `as Char`
Leaving non-alphabetic characters shifted — only letters should change
